h2: Custom NDT report templates and electronic signature sign-off
html:
Two phrases appear in almost every software comparison inspection companies read: customizable reporting and electronic signature. They matter because an NDT report is a controlled record. Your clients, their third-party inspectors and your own written practice all expect a report in a set format, signed by a qualified person, and traceable to the procedure, the calibration and the technician's certificate.

Custom NDT report templates, per method

A UT thickness survey, a shear-wave weld report, an MT report and a radiograph interpretation sheet do not share fields, so one generic form pushes technicians into free text and reviewers into checking it line by line. In the NDT Reports app each method has its own report type with its own fields and numbering, and the output is your template: your header and layout, or your client's where they insist on one, with the references your procedures call for, such as procedure and revision, technique sheet, calibration block, instrument and probe serials, acceptance standard and results. Adjusting a template is configuration work, not a new product.

What makes an electronic signature defensible

An auditor will ask who signed, whether that person was qualified to sign on that day, and whether the report changed afterwards. A signature carries weight only when the signer is a named user with their own login, their certificate for that method and level is on record, and the report's approval state is recorded with it. In the app a report moves through draft, review and approval; the approver signs at approval, and on client and code work the third-party or Authorized Inspector's name and signature can be recorded on the same report. The record then shows when the report was sent.

Level II performs, Level III reviews

Under an SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 written practice, the Level II who performed the examination records and signs the results, and the written practice decides who reviews and approves them, often a Level III for procedure-critical work. Building that rule into the workflow is what turns NDT reporting software into part of the quality system rather than a word processor. When you do not employ a Level III, the review step can be assigned to an outside one; see ASNT Level III consulting.

Offline in the field

Readings are captured on a tablet or phone through an installable web app that works offline. Drafts and photographs stay on the device and sync when a connection returns, so there is no clipboard to re-type at the end of the shift.

Where it fits

Reports draw technicians from the certification register and instruments from equipment and calibration tracking, and approved reports feed invoicing in the NDT management software. For other tools, see the NDT reporting software comparison. To see your own report formats configured, book a demonstration.
